categories.name: Graphics
categories.description: Comprehensive Graphics driver validation tests covering driver installation/PnP, display configuration, performance, power management, hybrid graphics, video processing, error handling (including TDR), and application compatibility for Surface devices (WDDM-focused).

sub-categories.name: Plug and Play
sub-categories.description: Tests specific to basic functionality of start/stop/disable/enable requests and resource handling by the Plug and Play infrastructure (PnP) for the graphics driver/adapter.

sub-categories.name: Display Configuration Support Tests
sub-categories.description: Tests to validate that the graphics driver under test supports different display configurations (multi-monitor, resolution/mode switches, external displays via USB-C/Surface Connect, hot-plug) as well as basic display functionality (brightness, ambient light sensor, etc.). Many tests use a Microsoft Surface Dock (port replicator; solid black brick form factor). Use only official Microsoft Surface Dock hardware; other port replicators are not supported for these validation scenarios.

sub-categories.name: DirectX Support
sub-categories.description: Tests to validate graphics driver support for different DirectX / DXGI feature levels, presentation models (blt/flip/DirectFlip), and related rendering functionality.

sub-categories.name: OpenGL/OpenCL Support
sub-categories.description: Tests to validate graphics driver support for OpenGL and OpenCL applications and related compute/rendering scenarios.

sub-categories.name: Power Management
sub-categories.description: Tests specific to basic functionality of power management scenarios (Sleep, Hibernate, Reboot, connected standby / Modern Standby where applicable, and graphics power-component handling).

sub-categories.name: Hybrid Graphics Support
sub-categories.description: Tests specific to hybrid graphics configurations (iGPU + dGPU) to verify interaction, cross-adapter resources, present paths, and switching between integrated and discrete graphics drivers.

sub-categories.name: Video Processing
sub-categories.description: Tests specific to verify graphics driver support for video processing scenarios (DXVA, video processor, decode/encode, playback under load, etc.).

sub-categories.name: Error Support
sub-categories.description: Tests specific to verify the robustness of the graphics driver when invalid parameters are intentionally sent to the driver, plus recovery support for timeout detection and recovery (TDR) and related error-handling scenarios.

sub-categories.name: Streaming + PM
sub-categories.description: Tests specific to power-state behavior (Sleep/Hibernate/connected standby) during video streaming scenarios using popular browsers and applications.

categories.name: Display
categories.description: Display User Experience Smoke Tests focused on visual quality, color accuracy, inking performance, brightness/ALS behavior, power-state visual consistency, and user-facing display features on Surface devices.

sub-categories.name: Accelerated Ink Functionality for primary apps
sub-categories.description: Tests for pen and finger inking performance, smoothness, latency, pressure sensitivity, and reliability in first-party Microsoft applications (Microsoft Edge, Snip & Sketch / Snipping Tool, Microsoft Whiteboard, and OneNote).

sub-categories.name: Color Profile Functionality and External Monitor
sub-categories.description: Tests related to color profile enumeration, validation, switching behavior, and correct application of color profiles on both the internal Surface display and external monitors.

sub-categories.name: Confirm Color Calibration
sub-categories.description: Verification of color calibration accuracy using UEFI tools and proper ICC profile handling and application on the display.

sub-categories.name: Driver Stability (Driver Verifier)
sub-categories.description: Stability testing with Driver Verifier enabled to detect memory corruption, leaks, and system crashes related to the display/graphics stack.

sub-categories.name: Enumeration and Control
sub-categories.description: Validation of monitor enumeration in Device Manager, correct driver loading and unloading, and basic display control functionality.

sub-categories.name: Image Quality
sub-categories.description: Visual validation tests for static images, video playback, text rendering, screen rotation, and multi-monitor / screen spanning scenarios.

sub-categories.name: Startup Behavior / State Transition
sub-categories.description: Validation of image consistency, brightness persistence, logo rendering, and overall visual behavior during power state transitions (boot, sleep, hibernate, and resume).

sub-categories.name: User Adjustment
sub-categories.description: Validation of user-facing display controls including Ambient Light Sensor (ALS) response, Night Light, Battery Saver effects on the display, brightness slider, and keyboard backlight brightness adjustment.

categories.name: Creativity
categories.description: Tests focused on creative applications performance, stability, and visual quality validation across 2D/3D drawing, rendering, Adobe Creative Cloud suite, video processing, and CAD tools on Surface devices.

sub-categories.name: 2D Drawing
sub-categories.description: Tests inking, sketching, photo editing, layering, and basic drawing capabilities using popular 2D creative applications, with emphasis on pen/touch performance, smoothness, and visual fidelity.

sub-categories.name: 3D Rendering
sub-categories.description: Evaluates 3D model viewing, creation, basic manipulation, rendering performance, and visual quality in 3D creative workflows.

sub-categories.name: Adobe
sub-categories.description: Comprehensive testing of Adobe Creative Cloud applications (Photoshop, Fresco, Lightroom, After Effects, Premiere Pro, Illustrator, and related tools) covering photo editing, sketching, layering, animation, compositing, and video workflows for performance, stability, and visual quality.

sub-categories.name: Video Processing
sub-categories.description: Validates professional video editing workflows including color adjustment, splicing, transitions, effects, playback, and export quality, primarily using Adobe tools and similar creative video applications.

sub-categories.name: Computer Aided Design
sub-categories.description: Assesses 3D modeling, design, and basic CAD workflows (viewing, editing, manipulation, and export) using applications such as FreeCAD, SketchUp, and comparable CAD tools.

categories.name: Gaming
categories.description: Validates gaming performance, core device functionality during gameplay, accessories support, third-party platform compatibility, and Mixed Reality gaming experiences on Surface devices.

sub-categories.name: Gaming Accessories
sub-categories.description: Tests functionality and reliability of gaming-related accessories including keyboard, mouse, Bluetooth headsets, Xbox controllers, and Type Cover during gameplay.

sub-categories.name: Device Functionality for Gaming
sub-categories.description: Core device gaming validation covering display configurations, audio output, touch input, Xbox Game Pass, game launch experience, fullscreen behavior, playability, frame rate (FPS), sleep/resume, detach scenarios, and Xbox Game Bar integration.

sub-categories.name: Third-Party Platforms Support
sub-categories.description: Installation, sign-in, game library access, and game launch validation for major third-party platforms including Steam, Battle.net (Blizzard), and Epic Games Launcher.

sub-categories.name: Mixed Reality Experience
sub-categories.description: Validates Mixed Reality setup and gaming experiences including Minecraft MR, Edge browsing in MR, video playback, home area navigation, motion controllers, sleep/resume behavior, audio, and overall MR session stability.

categories.name: BPM
categories.description: Validates Battery Protection Management (BPM) features across versions including smart charging, counters, protection modes, Battery Limit Mode, Charge Temperature Throttling, and health indicators.

sub-categories.name: BPM_1
sub-categories.description: Counter_A: The system shall increment a counter every minute when RSOC >= 81% over a rolling 7-day period using the table.

sub-categories.name: BPM_2
sub-categories.description: When exiting BPM, Counter_A shall be set to 0.

sub-categories.name: BPM_3
sub-categories.description: Counter_B: The system shall increment a counter every minute when RSOC > 95% and the device is in active/S0 power state.

sub-categories.name: BPM_4
sub-categories.description: When dropping below RSOC 93% and BPM is engaged, Counter B shall be set to 0.

sub-categories.name: BPM_5
sub-categories.description: Once either counter exceeds 3540 and RSOC >= 81%, the system shall enter Battery Protection Mode (BPM).

sub-categories.name: BPM_6
sub-categories.description: The system shall not enter BPM for the first time until the HvtLifeTime counter exceeds 10,620 minutes.

sub-categories.name: BPM_7

sub-categories.name: BPM_9
sub-categories.description: While in BPM, if the battery RSOC drops below 50%, the device shall exit BPM.

sub-categories.description: While in BPM, the true RSOC shall be shown to the user without scaling.

sub-categories.name: BPM_12
sub-categories.description: The user shall be able to pause BPM for 1 day or 7 days from the Surface App while on battery power or attached to AC power.

sub-categories.name: BPM_13

sub-categories.name: BPM_14
sub-categories.description: If a user selects a pause period while BPM is already paused, the remaining pause period should change to the newly selected duration.

sub-categories.name: BPM_15
sub-categories.description: The user shall be able to manually enter BPM and hold the device at an RSOC of 80% using the Surface App.

sub-categories.name: BPM_16
sub-categories.description: The system shall maintain the battery at an RSOC level of 80% with PSU attached, with a float charge of 77-80% while always showing 80%.

sub-categories.name: BPM_17
sub-categories.description: System will ignore the first 3 BPM entries.

sub-categories.name: BPM_18
sub-categories.description: Battery telemetry should reflect the current BPM state and counters while the device is in the protected mode.

sub-categories.name: BPM_19

sub-categories.name: BPM_20

categories.name: Consumption
categories.description: Battery, energy-efficiency, and media-experience validation for sustained media-consumption workloads on Microsoft Surface and Windows devices. This category covers approved Windows-client and browser paths for streaming video, streaming audio, and media-rich feeds. It evaluates battery discharge and runtime consistency, display and audio power use, network streaming activity, hardware-accelerated media decoding, graphics and media-driver behavior, DRM-protected playback, thermal and stability behavior, playback quality, and application or browser UX. Map issues here when media consumption is the primary workload or trigger. Connected or Modern Standby is relevant only to explicit screen-off, background-audio, suspend/resume, or power-transition variants. Exact content titles, accounts, regions, service tiers, codecs, resolutions, brightness, volume, network conditions, software builds, and driver versions must be maintained as execution metadata in the authoritative test procedure.

sub-categories.name: Netflix (1hrs - The Office/Walking Dead)
sub-categories.description: Run approved Netflix video through the designated Windows client for a nominal one-hour battery workload with the display active. Playback should remain stable, responsive, synchronized, and power efficient while using the expected DRM, network, audio, display, and hardware-decoding paths. Validate battery discharge and media quality. Map Netflix-client issues involving abnormal drain, startup failure, buffering, DRM, decode acceleration, artifacts, A/V sync, crashes, thermal behavior, windowing, or resume recovery.

sub-categories.name: Amazon Video (1hrs - The Grand Tour)
sub-categories.description: Stream approved Prime Video content through the designated Windows client for one hour on battery. The Surface device should sustain protected playback without excessive power use, instability, visual corruption, audio defects, or repeated buffering. Validate runtime consistency across the media, graphics, display, audio, and Wi-Fi paths. Map Prime Video client defects involving battery drain, DRM authorization, playback startup, hardware decoding, A/V synchronization, captions, window transitions, crashes, or recovery.

sub-categories.name: Hulu  (1hrs - Modern Family)
sub-categories.description: Run an approved Hulu video workload in the designated Windows client for one hour on battery with the screen active. Playback should remain smooth and synchronized while the device efficiently uses network, protected-media, decode, graphics, audio, and display resources. Map Hulu-client issues involving excessive discharge, launch or sign-in-to-playback failures, buffering, DRM, dropped frames, artifacts, captions, full-screen behavior, crashes, thermal escalation, or sleep/resume recovery.

sub-categories.name: HBO Max (1hrs - Game of Thrones)
sub-categories.description: Play an approved YouTube video through the designated Windows client or installed PWA for one hour on battery. The workload should use efficient video decoding and maintain stable adaptive streaming, audio/video synchronization, rendering, and user controls. Validate battery drain, display activity, network use, and media quality. Map issues involving abnormal power use, buffering, resolution switching, dropped frames, artifacts, hardware acceleration, full-screen transitions, captions, crashes, or resume behavior.

sub-categories.name: Disney + (1hr -Spiderman)
sub-categories.description: Execute the baseline HBO Max Windows-client workload using an approved standard playback profile for one hour on battery. Expect stable protected video, synchronized audio, responsive controls, and consistent power consumption under the standard quality configuration. Map baseline-profile issues involving battery regression, playback startup, DRM, buffering, decode or graphics behavior, artifacts, captions, windowing, crashes, or recovery. This entry is distinct from the protected higher-quality profile in sub-category 6.

sub-categories.name: Facebook (20min )
sub-categories.description: Execute a second HBO Max Windows-client workload using the approved protected or higher-quality media profile supported by the device, account, region, title, and display. Validate DRM robustness, hardware-protected playback where available, higher media-pipeline load, display behavior, and battery efficiency. Map issues specific to protected playback, quality escalation, HD or HDR negotiation when supported, black video, DRM errors, elevated CPU or GPU use, excessive drain, artifacts, or instability.

sub-categories.name: Netflix (New Microsoft Edge)
sub-categories.description: Stream approved Disney+ video through the designated Windows client for one hour on battery. Playback should remain stable and synchronized while the platform efficiently uses protected-media, network, hardware-decode, graphics, audio, and display paths. Validate battery consumption and user-visible media quality. Map Disney+ client issues involving abnormal drain, DRM, startup, buffering, artifacts, dropped frames, A/V sync, captions, window or full-screen behavior, crashes, thermal behavior, or resume recovery.

categories.name: Audio
categories.description: Audio covers end-to-end Microsoft Surface audio validation across the Windows audio subsystem and user experience, including audio driver packages, codecs, miniports, services, Audio Processing Objects (APOs), DSP and offload processing, internal speakers, microphone arrays, audio enhancements, voice processing, wired and wireless endpoints, Bluetooth Classic and LE Audio, USB and USB-C audio, Surface Dock and display-audio paths, endpoint discovery and routing, format and sample-rate support, stream concurrency, power-state behavior, real-time communications, speech and accessibility experiences, Microsoft Edge media streaming, and application-specific playback and capture. Validation targets correct installation, enumeration, routing, processing, persistence, audio quality, latency, synchronization, controls, power transitions, interoperability, and recovery. Issues include missing or unstable endpoints, no or low audio, incorrect routing, distortion, imbalance, echo, noise, feedback, clipping, pops, clicks, dropouts, glitches, latency, audio-video desynchronization, setting-persistence failures, service or driver failures, crashes, hangs, and regressions after driver, firmware, operating-system, accessory, or application changes.

sub-categories.name: Drivers
sub-categories.description: Covers validation of the Microsoft Surface audio software package and its integration with Windows and platform hardware, including audio bus, codec and miniport drivers, component and extension drivers, display-audio drivers, Bluetooth and USB audio dependencies, Audio Processing Objects (APOs), DSP integration, audio services, companion applications, firmware interfaces, and driver-delivered endpoint topology or configuration. Validate clean-image installation, side-load and Windows Update paths, update, rollback, uninstall and reinstall, version and date, signatures and INF correctness, service startup, device enumeration, endpoint availability, reboot and power-transition recovery, stream creation, APO initialization and data flow, system stability, and applicable HLK or certification requirements. Map issues here when the primary failure is driver-package installation or servicing, a missing or warning-state device, incorrect version, broken enumeration or topology, service or APO activation failure, driver or firmware incompatibility, crash, hang, bugcheck, memory or resource fault, or an audio regression introduced by a driver, firmware, or operating-system update. Application-only behavior and otherwise healthy platform features belong in their respective workload categories.

sub-categories.name: Features
sub-categories.description: Covers platform-level Microsoft Surface audio capabilities and cross-workload behavior independent of a single communications client, website, or application. Scope includes built-in speakers and microphone arrays; microphone directionality and beamforming; acoustic echo cancellation, noise suppression, automatic gain control, Voice Clarity and Voice Focus; Dolby and spatial-audio technologies; equalization, virtualization and volume leveling; Personal Audio Sharing; Bluetooth Classic and Bluetooth LE Audio; 3.5 mm, USB and USB-C audio; Surface Dock and HDMI or DisplayPort audio paths; endpoint discovery, default-device selection and transitions; channel balance, volume and media-key behavior; formats, sample rates and bit depths; stream concurrency; audio-video synchronization; offload and low-power playback; orientation, attach or detach behavior; setting persistence; and Modern Standby, sleep, hibernate, reboot and resume scenarios, where supported. Validate clear, balanced, continuous and correctly processed render and capture audio, correct endpoint routing and switching, control responsiveness, feature enablement and persistence, synchronization, interoperability and reliable recovery. Map cross-application issues such as distortion, clipping, imbalance, echo, noise, feedback, dropouts, incorrect processing, unsupported formats, wrong endpoint selection, failed transitions, PAS synchronization failures or power-state regressions here; map package or enumeration defects to Drivers and workload-specific failures to Communication, Edge Browser Streaming or Applications.

sub-categories.name: Communication
sub-categories.description: Covers real-time communications, conversational audio, Windows speech and related accessibility workloads on Microsoft Surface, including voice and video calls in clients such as Microsoft Teams, Zoom, Webex and similar services, as well as Narrator, Voice Access, voice typing, dictation, speech recognition and other communication-oriented accessibility experiences. Validate full-duplex capture and render through built-in speakers and microphone arrays, wired headsets, USB or USB-C devices, Bluetooth Classic and LE Audio devices, and display or Surface Dock output combined with the intended microphone input. Expected behavior includes correct device discovery and selection, intelligible two-way audio, stable communications processing such as beamforming, acoustic echo cancellation, noise suppression, automatic gain control, Voice Focus or Voice Clarity where supported, correct Bluetooth communications mode, mute and unmute, call and media controls, endpoint switching, notifications, concurrent media, power transitions and recovery. Map issues such as one-way or missing call audio, echo, feedback, excessive noise, robotic or distorted speech, low microphone level, dropouts, latency, wrong input or output selection, Bluetooth profile or quality changes, failed mute state, speech-recognition failure or communication-specific endpoint transitions here. Browser-hosted media playback belongs in Edge Browser Streaming, and non-communications application audio belongs in Applications.

sub-categories.name: Edge Browser Streaming
sub-categories.description: Covers website-hosted audio and video media playback in Microsoft Edge on Microsoft Surface, including music, video, protected or DRM-controlled content, adaptive or high-quality streams, and representative services such as YouTube, Netflix, Disney+, Hulu, Amazon and Spotify web experiences. Validate playback through built-in speakers, 3.5 mm, USB or USB-C, Bluetooth Classic, Bluetooth LE Audio, external display and Surface Dock audio paths; codec and format handling; protected-content playback; audio quality and continuity; audio-video synchronization; hardware, system and webpage volume controls; play, pause, resume, seek and mute; tab, window, foreground and background transitions; endpoint arrival, removal and switching; concurrent tabs or streams; network interruption and recovery; and supported sleep, Modern Standby or resume behavior. Map issues here when they reproduce specifically during media consumption in Microsoft Edge, including no sound, playback stalls, distorted or intermittent audio, lip-sync errors, control failures, DRM or codec-related playback failures, incorrect browser endpoint routing, loss of audio after seek or tab switching, or browser-specific power-state regressions. Real-time browser calls remain Communication, and the same symptom in an installed application belongs in Applications.

sub-categories.name: Applications
sub-categories.description: Covers application-specific Microsoft Surface audio playback, capture and control behavior outside website-hosted Microsoft Edge media and dedicated real-time communications workloads. Scope includes Windows inbox, Microsoft Store, desktop and media applications such as Media Player, Movies and TV, streaming-service apps, Spotify, Camera, Sound Recorder, Copilot voice experiences and other applications that render, record, process or respond to audio. Validate local and streamed content, application startup and recovery, supported codecs, containers, channels, formats and sample rates, microphone selection and recording, playback quality, hardware and software volume, play, pause, resume, seek and mute, endpoint selection and transitions across built-in, wired, USB or USB-C, Bluetooth, LE Audio, external display and Surface Dock paths, application concurrency, background and foreground behavior, accessibility output, and supported sleep, Modern Standby, detach, resume and reboot scenarios. Map issues here when audio behavior is isolated to a particular non-Edge application, including no playback or capture, wrong endpoint, silent or corrupted recording, distorted or intermittent audio, format failure, broken media controls, incorrect persistence, application-specific latency or synchronization, or failure after an application lifecycle or power event. Cross-application platform defects belong in Features, package or enumeration failures in Drivers, and call or speech collaboration failures in Communication.

categories.name: Touch
categories.description: Validates the integrated touchscreen digitizer and the touch-related user experience on Microsoft Surface devices, including finger contact detection, supported multi-touch gestures, contact tracking, accuracy, responsiveness, palm rejection, and interaction with Surface Pen where the pen and touchscreen share the display digitizer path. Coverage includes Windows, supported Surface UEFI experiences, applicable device postures, Type Cover attachment states, power transitions, applications, and touch-related reliability signals. Use this category for defects in which finger or pen input is missing, inaccurate, delayed, unstable, falsely generated, incorrectly interpreted, or affected by a Surface or Windows state transition. Exclude touchpad-only defects, display image-quality defects with no input impact, and unrelated Bluetooth, application, or accessory failures unless they directly cause or expose a touchscreen or digitizer problem.

sub-categories.name: Functional Tests
sub-categories.description: Validates whether the Surface touchscreen digitizer and related pen-input path provide the expected fundamental capabilities. Coverage includes device availability and enumeration, single-touch and simultaneous multi-touch detection, continuous contact tracking, full-screen and edge coverage, taps, presses, dragging, swiping, panning, pinch and rotation gestures, contact release, and rejection of phantom or unintended contacts. It also covers supported Surface Pen tip, eraser, hover, pressure-related input, palm rejection, and pen-touch arbitration when those behaviors depend on the integrated digitizer. Surface-specific validation includes touch operation in Surface UEFI where supported and basic operation across applicable Type Cover attachment states and device postures. Route an issue here when a basic input capability is absent, reports the wrong contact state, loses tracking, creates false contacts, or fails consistently independent of a particular application's implementation. Route primarily timing, smoothness, precision, or sustained user-experience degradation to Responsiveness and Usability Tests instead.

sub-categories.name: Power Management and Resume Tests
sub-categories.description: Validates that touchscreen and supported pen input enter, leave, and recover from Windows and Surface power states without loss of functionality, false input, excessive recovery delay, or abnormal power behavior. Coverage includes display-off transitions, sleep, Modern Standby including scenarios historically described as Connected Standby, hibernate, restart, shutdown and cold boot, repeated suspend and resume cycles, and operation on AC power and battery power. Applicable Surface scenarios include Type Cover attached or detached, supported docking or undocking transitions, lid or posture changes, and recovery after firmware or driver servicing. Wake-on-Touch is validated only on devices and configurations that explicitly support it; failure to wake must not be assumed to be a defect on unsupported devices, and pen contact is not treated as a Wake-on-Touch mechanism. Route an issue here when touch or pen behavior depends on a power-state transition, wake source, input-suppression state, power source, or resume sequence. Route input failures that occur continuously in the fully active state to Functional Tests or Responsiveness and Usability Tests.

sub-categories.name: Responsiveness and Usability Tests
sub-categories.description: Evaluates the quality, timing, precision, stability, and practical usability of touchscreen and digitizer input after basic functionality has been established. Coverage includes response latency, report-rate consistency, jitter, lag, stutter, line wobble, tracking smoothness, contact separation, spatial accuracy, edge and corner usability, fast or repeated gestures, long drags, sustained inking, accidental-contact rejection, and consistency across display orientation, scaling, resolution, and supported device postures. Surface-specific scenarios include changes caused by Type Cover attachment or detachment, convertible or tablet posture, supported external-display or Dock transitions, and peripheral, power, or environmental interactions that degrade touch or pen usability. Windows 10 tablet-mode behavior and Windows 11 posture-responsive behavior must be evaluated according to the operating system and device under test rather than treated as identical features. Route an issue here when touch or pen works but feels delayed, inaccurate, unstable, inconsistent, or difficult to use. Route complete loss of a capability to Functional Tests, power-transition-specific failures to Power Management and Resume Tests, and behavior isolated to an application's input handling to Application Support Tests.

sub-categories.name: Application Support Tests
sub-categories.description: Validates compatibility and end-to-end touchscreen and pen workflows in Windows shell experiences and supported first-party or third-party applications after the underlying digitizer has been shown to function. Coverage includes activating controls, selecting content, scrolling, panning, zooming, rotating, dragging and dropping, text selection, touch-keyboard invocation where applicable, drawing, inking, erasing, supported pressure-sensitive input, palm rejection, and switching between touch, pen, keyboard, and mouse interaction. Validation should consider windowed and full-screen use, orientation and DPI changes, app switching, application suspend and resume, and differences between drawing canvases, browsers, document editors, productivity applications, and Windows user-interface surfaces. The Surface App may be included when it configures or diagnoses a supported pen or touch experience, but unrelated Surface App defects do not belong here. Route an issue here when the touchscreen or pen works at the platform level but an application, control, or application class interprets or responds to the input incorrectly. A system-wide failure across applications should be routed to Functional Tests, Responsiveness and Usability Tests, or Power Management and Resume Tests according to the observed behavior.

sub-categories.name: Touch Telemetry
sub-categories.description: Covers touch and pen reliability, servicing, and customer-impact signals identified through telemetry or fleet-level diagnostic analysis rather than through a single manual functional test. This includes evidence of touchscreen or digitizer driver installation failures, device-start problems, firmware or driver regressions, repeated touch-stack faults, abnormal recovery patterns, failures correlated with device model, operating-system build, power state, or update deployment, and trends indicating degraded touch or pen health. Telemetry findings should be associated with the affected touch component, Surface model, driver or firmware version, Windows state, and observable customer impact when that information is available. Route an issue here when its primary evidence is aggregate monitoring, deployment health, diagnostic events, or reliability signals. Do not use this sub-category merely because logs or traces were collected for an otherwise reproducible functional, responsiveness, power-management, or application-specific defect.

sub-categories.name: NFC

sub-categories.name: OwnerSignerConfiguration

sub-categories.name: PXEBootIPv6

sub-categories.name: SDCard

sub-categories.name: SDEBuildUSB

sub-categories.name: SDTLogSave

categories.name: MSI
categories.description: Validates Microsoft Surface Windows Installer (MSI) packages used to deploy cumulative driver and firmware updates to supported Surface devices. This category covers package applicability, integrity, installation and servicing behavior, driver and firmware staging, restart-dependent completion, deployment reporting, and verification that the intended payloads reach the correct installed state. It includes Surface-specific components such as graphics, battery, System Aggregator Module, embedded controller, UEFI, keyboard or Type Cover, and Surface Dock content only when those components are included in or explicitly targeted by the package. Issues should be classified under MSI when the primary failure concerns package composition, model or operating-system applicability, installation, upgrade, repair, removal, deployment, logging, restart handling, or the immediate post-install state. Functional defects that remain after the correct package and payload have installed successfully should be classified under the affected component or feature category instead.

sub-categories.name: Installation and Servicing Functionality
sub-categories.description: Validates the end-to-end behavior of a Surface driver and firmware MSI throughout its supported installation and servicing lifecycle. Testing verifies that the package starts and completes correctly in interactive, unattended, and enterprise deployment contexts; evaluates the current device, processor architecture, Windows release, and build for applicability; stages driver packages in the Driver Store; binds intended drivers to matching devices; stages included firmware for restart-dependent activation; and communicates success, failure, or restart requirements accurately through installer status and diagnostic logs. It also verifies supported reinstall, upgrade, repair, rollback, and removal behavior where applicable, including recovery from interruption or failure without leaving partially installed payloads, unresolved devices, repeated installation requests, or an unstable system state. Post-installation validation confirms that expected devices enumerate without deployment-related errors, intended driver and firmware versions are reported after any required restart, and installation results remain consistent across shutdown, startup, sleep, resume, and subsequent update detection. Surface accessories or platform components, including Surface Dock, Type Cover or keyboard, battery, System Aggregator Module, embedded controller, UEFI, graphics, and other device-specific hardware, are included only when the MSI contains or targets their update payloads.

sub-categories.name: Package Content and Applicability Validation
sub-categories.description: Validates that a Surface MSI contains the complete, correct, trustworthy, and properly targeted set of driver, firmware, and supporting installation content for the intended Surface model and Windows configuration. Testing compares the package against the approved release definition and verifies expected MSI metadata, driver INF files, catalog files, signed binaries, firmware payloads, version information, providers, device classes, hardware targeting, dependencies, and supporting resources. It confirms that digital signatures and catalog relationships are valid; package content is not corrupt or altered; all required payloads are present; and no unintended, stale, duplicate, superseded, or incompatible drivers or firmware are included. Applicability validation verifies alignment with the intended Surface product, processor architecture, Windows release and build, and device-specific hardware configuration, and confirms that unsupported systems are rejected without modification. After installation and any required restart, the versions and device state reported by Windows must correspond to the package contents, with no missing devices, unexpected component changes, unresolved driver associations, or firmware remaining incomplete. Surface-specific payloads such as System Aggregator Module, embedded controller, UEFI, battery, graphics, keyboard or Type Cover, and Surface Dock are validated when present, but detailed behavioral testing of those components belongs to their respective functional categories once correct package installation has been established.

categories.name: Image BVT
categories.description: Covers build verification, qualification, and release-readiness validation of a newly created Microsoft Surface or Windows device image before it is made available for broader automated, self-host, or collateral testing. This category applies to issues involving image composition, pre-install integrity, deployment to a Device Under Test (DUT), first boot, Windows build identity, integrated driver and firmware payloads, device enumeration, release metadata, validation logs, baseline preservation, and final image sign-off. It includes failures caused by missing, extra, incorrect, stale, mismatched, or nonfunctional components in the integrated image, as well as installation, boot, configuration, and release-gating problems. It does not represent detailed functional testing of an individual feature such as graphics, battery management, Surface Dock, Type Cover, ambient light sensing, Connected Standby, audio, camera, networking, or Surface application behavior after the image baseline has been verified. It is also distinct from Windows Hardware Lab Kit certification testing, although an HLK failure may be associated with this category when it directly demonstrates a defect in the packaged or deployed image.

sub-categories.name: Image Build Verification and Sign-off
sub-categories.description: Validates that a newly produced device image is complete, deployable, correctly configured, and suitable for release to downstream testing. Pre-install validation confirms that the image contains the expected operating-system content, driver and firmware packages, INF identities and versions, manifests, registry configuration, release notes, version-information files, scripts, tools, and other required artifacts. It covers missing or corrupted files, incomplete package staging, incorrect folder structure, manifest-to-image discrepancies, incorrect Railcar or build metadata, and mismatches between the approved component table and the payload included in the image. Deployment validation confirms that the image can be installed through the applicable automated or USB-based process on the intended Surface Device Under Test, completes Windows setup without unexpected failure, rollback, recovery, or blocking prompt, and boots reliably to a usable Windows desktop. Post-install validation confirms the expected Windows edition, version, build, architecture, image or Railcar identity, and device configuration. It verifies that planned driver and firmware changes are present and active by comparing the approved component definition with Device Manager, VersionInformation.txt, driver-verification reports, applicable Surface UEFI or BIOS information, release notes, and other build evidence. It includes detection of missing devices, unexpected devices, unresolved Device Manager warning or error states, driver load or start failures, incorrect driver provider, INF, version, or date, firmware-version mismatches, improperly applied firmware capsules, stale or unintended packages, and differences between packaged and installed content. Validation also covers review of setup, driver, payload-comparison, and device-health logs, including failures or warnings that require investigation before release. Sign-off requires successful installation, stable boot, correct build identity, expected payload presence and activation, healthy enumeration of applicable Surface hardware, consistent release metadata, acceptable validation results, and no unresolved release-blocking defect. Any expected exception or waiver must be reviewed and documented rather than assumed to be acceptable. After BVT passes, the validated baseline must be protected from unintended Windows Update, driver, firmware, or servicing changes before collateral execution so that subsequent results remain attributable to the signed-off image. Issues should be assigned here when they concern the integrity, deployment, integrated payload correctness, baseline health, or release readiness of the complete image. Feature-specific functional defects found after the image baseline is confirmed should be assigned to the corresponding graphics, power, battery, firmware, input, Dock, sensor, connectivity, application, or other functional category.
